==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:der|la:agēns|tree=1}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eǵ-|id=drive}}
From {{der|en|la|agēns}}, present active participle of {{m|la|ago|agere|to drive, lead, conduct, manage, perform, do}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈeɪ̯d͡ʒənt/|[ˈeɪ̯d͡ʒənt]|~|[ˈeɪ̯d͡ʒn̩t]}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-agent.ogg|a=US}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-agent.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{hyph|en|a|gent}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|person who exerts or has power to act}} One who exerts power, or has the power to [[act]].
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1862|author=Brigham Young|work=Journal of Discourses|volume=9|title=Call for Teams to Go to the Frontiers, etc.|passage=Seeing we are so wonderfully endowed with priceless gifts by our Heavenly Father, will he not require usury at our hands? He will. But he has made us '''agents''' to ourselves, which makes us responsible for the way in which we use the talents he has given us, for the manner we expend the gold and silver, the wheat and fine flour, the cattle upon a thousand hills, and the wine and oil, for they all belong to Him}}
# {{senseid|en|person who acts by proxy for another}} {{lb|en|law}} One who acts for, or in the place of, another (the [[principal]]), by that person's authority; someone [[entrust]]ed to act [[on behalf of]] or [[in behalf of]] another, such as to transact business for them.
#: {{ux|en|He worked as an '''agent''' for the government.}}
#* {{RQ:Melville Moby-Dick|chapter=36|passage=I see in him [Moby Dick] outrageous strength, with an inscrutable malice sinewing it. That inscrutable thing is chiefly what I hate; and be the white whale '''agent''', or be the white whale principal, I will wreak that hate upon him.}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Jeanne Sahadi|title=What a buyer’s agent will do for you when you’re looking for a new home|url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/04/22/success/buyers-agent-real-estate-obligations|date=2024-04-22|passage=Having a good buyer’s '''agent''' also means having someone who is knowledgeable about the local real estate market and who has the skills and competence to negotiate with the seller’s '''agent''' on your behalf.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250118023249/https://www.cnn.com/2024/04/22/success/buyers-agent-real-estate-obligations}}
# {{senseid|en|person who finds and arranges work for another}} A person who looks for work for another person and brokers a deal between the [[hiree]] and [[hirer]].
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=2016-06-04|author=Press Association|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/jun/04/ronald-koeman-reportedly-everton-terms-agreed-southampton|title=Ronald Koeman’s agent says Dutchman has agreed terms with Everton|passage={{w|Ronald Koeman}} has agreed a deal with Everton to become their new manager, his '''agent''' has reportedly told Dutch media. The '''agent''' Rob Jansen said, according to the popular Voetbal International website, that it was now down to Southampton and Everton to agree a compensation package for the Dutchman, who has a year remaining on his contract at St Mary’s.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210622225403/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/jun/04/ronald-koeman-reportedly-everton-terms-agreed-southampton}}
# {{senseid|en|person who helps with intelligence gathering}} Someone who works for an [[intelligence agency]]: whether an [[officer]] or [[employee]] thereof or anyone else who agrees to help their efforts (for [[ideology]], for [[money]], as [[blackmailee]], or otherwise).
# {{senseid|en|active power or cause or substance}} An active power or cause or substance; something (e.g. biological, chemical, thermal, etc.) that has the power to produce an effect.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1807|author=James Edward Smith|title=An introduction to physiological and systematical botany|chapter=11
|passage=So far seems to be the work of chemistry alone; at least we have no right to conclude that any other '''agent''' interferes; since hay, when it happens to imbibe moisture, exhibits nearly the same processes."}}
# {{senseid|en|aid to client or server in computing}} {{lb|en|computing}} In the [[client-server]] model, the part of the system that performs information preparation and exchange on behalf of a [[client]] or [[server]]. Especially in the phrase “intelligent agent” it implies some kind of autonomous process which can communicate with other agents to perform some collective task on behalf of one or more humans.
#* {{RQ:FT|edition=weekend|title=AI enters the house: ‘It's a total game-changer’|date=2026-09-05|page=6|section=Life & Arts|author=Valeriya Safronova|passage=[Jesse] Genet uses five AI '''agents''' to manage her seven-child household on a ranch outside Los Angeles.}}
# {{senseid|en|grammar}} {{lb|en|grammar}} The participant of a situation that carries out the action in this situation, e.g. "the boy" in the sentences "The boy kicked the ball" and "The ball was kicked by the boy".
#: {{ant|en|patient<id:linguistics>}}
#: {{cot|en|subject<id:n-grammar>|object<id:n-grammar>|;|rheme<id:linguistics>|theme<id:linguistic counterpart to rheme>}}
#: {{nearsyn|en|doer#Noun}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2009|author=Tarsee Li|title=The Verbal System of the Aramaic of Daniel: An Explanation in the Context of Grammaticalization|page=58
|passage=A verb is typically described as active when its subject is the '''agent''' or actor. By contrast, a verb is said to be passive when the subject does not perform the action, but is the patient, target, or undergoer of the action.}}
# {{senseid|en|cheater with insider help in gambling}} {{lb|en|gambling}} A [[cheat]] who is assisted by [[dishonest]] [[casino]] [[staff]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1978|author=John Scarne|title=Scarne's guide to casino gambling|page=108
|passage=Nevada casinos are fleeced out of millions of dollars yearly by '''agents''' (cheats acting as players) in collusion with crooked Black Jack dealers and pit bosses.}}
# {{lb|en|US|}} A law enforcement officer tasked with enforcing a specific field of law.
#: {{ux|en|The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives officers are just simply referred to as "ATF '''agents'''".}}
#: {{ux|en|All federal '''agents''' are federal police officers but not all federal police officers are '''agents'''. For example, Drug Enforcement Administration '''agents''' are both '''agents''' and federal police officers while US Marshals are just federal police officers.}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Priscilla Alvarez; Rosa Flores|title=Trump administration launches nationwide immigration enforcement blitz|url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/01/26/politics/chicago-immigration-trump-ice/index.html|date=2025-01-26|passage=In the Atlanta suburb of Lilburn, ICE '''agents''' arrested Walter Valladares, a 53-year-old undocumented immigrant from Honduras, according to family members who spoke with CNN.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250309132730/https://www.cnn.com/2025/01/26/politics/chicago-immigration-trump-ice/index.html}}
# {{senseid|en|term of address}} {{lb|en|usually|US|capitalized}} {{n-g|A [[respectful]] [[term]] of [[address]] for an agent, especially a [[law enforcement]] agent.}}
#* {{quote-video game|en|year=2013|author=w:Rockstar Games|title=w:Grand Theft Auto V|system=|level=The Wrap Up|scene=Standoff between Michael de Santa and Steve Haines|text='''Steve Haines ({{w|Robert Bogue}})''': '''Agent''' Sanchez! Apprehend these suspects!}}
